title: Lara Trump brutally mocked as she exposes what happens at Trump family dinners - NewsBreak
text:
By Hannah Furnell Jorge Solis ,
45 minutes ago Although Lara Trump offered a rare glimpse into life within the Trump family, her revelations were met with skepticism from some quarters.
On Tuesday, April 21, the 43-year-old Fox News host — President Donald Trump 's daughter-in-law and the wife of Eric Trump — shared some surprising details about the president and her parenting philosophy during an appearance on The Katie Miller Podcast. Lara also revealed what family meals are like for the Trump clan.
"They're absolutely hilarious," Lara said of Trump family dinners. Yet numerous viewers have voiced their skepticism about the mother-of-two's assertions. In the comments section of Miller's Instagram post discussing Lara's remarks, one social media user wrote, "Sure...." This follows closely after Lara disclosed information about her notoriously private brother-in-law Barron Trump's personal life.
• Netflix's Elizabeth Smart unveils bodybuilder transformation after horror ordeal
• Fox News viewers fume 'she'll burn in hell' as Karoline Leavitt issues four-word jab
When Miller inquired about what family dinners entail, Lara responded, "They're absolutely hilarious. I mean, it's so entertaining. It kind of runs the gamut. You hear the president talk about how he'll, like, start on a subject and go all the way around the weave he calls it.
"I feel like we do that at every family dinner, like weaves around. So we start on one topic and then it goes crazy and everyone's laughing. And he's a consummate storyteller." Lara concluded. "But it's funny. It's a good time. It's always lighthearted and fun."
Miller captioned her clip of the moment with, "Turns out Trump family dinners are HILARIOUS," sparking a flood of reactions from both her and Lara's followers, reports the Irish Star .
Skepticism ran high in the comments, with one user writing, "Yeah, right, Lara... we believe every word you say." Another sarcastically responded, "Oh I'm sure lol," while a third flatly stated, "They don't have family dinners." A fifth shared a GIF of actor John Candy saying, "Oh sure, sure."
The doubters kept coming, with one user penning, "Like she would ever tell the truth about the family dinners or rather the family dinners they don't have. Looking kind of run down these days girl." Another chimed in, "They don't have family dinners! They are all a bunch of lying grifters!!" One commenter raged, "DO YOU ACTUALLY BELIEVE THE LIES YOU SPEW!!?" while yet another took a different angle, writing, "The Weave... He couldn't stay on topic if he wanted to."
Not everyone was critical, however. Some came to Lara's defense, with one supporter asking, "Yeah everyone in the comments is so perfect right?! And your family dinners are all rainbows and butterflies? I'm sure you all have no room to judge." Others simply backed her up with comments like "Nothing but facts," and "Yes sir. Great family. Patriots."
The controversy didn't end there, as Lara also faced backlash following a bold claim she made about Trump on Miller's podcast, asserting that her father-in-law suffered financially during his time serving as POTUS. The revelation came when Miller asked her, "What's something about your father-in-law that you wish more people knew that you haven't said publicly?"
Lara replied, "I mean, I kind of feel like I've said it all publicly. I wish people knew that his life, and I just wish people would appreciate, especially people on the other side of the aisle, how much easier his life would have been if he'd never gotten involved in politics. He's the one president to leave the White House with less money than he went into it with.
"He's had zeros off his net worth come off because he became president, because he ran for president. You know they've gone after his businesses, they've gone after his family. His life prior to politics, I mean, my gosh, everybody loved Donald Trump. But he's an incredibly genuine, good-hearted person.
"He's doing what he thinks is right, and I remember him saying to all of us, before he even ran and announced in 2015, 'You know what, if I do this, I'm going to do it the right way, and if it means I only get one term in office, then that's okay with me.' He's also one of the funniest people I've ever met. Anybody who is around him knows that," she finished.
Lara's remarks drew criticism from detractors who took to social media to challenge her statements. One X user posted, "Not true. His net worth dropped from 3.7B before his first term down to 2.5B by the end of it in 2021, due to the pandemic. During his 2nd term his wealth rebounded to 6.5B." A second viewer commented, "But then he got elected and manipulated the stock market and gave grace to crypto criminals and is six billion richer. Keep on telling me how this simp is suffering."
A third chimed in with, "Straight up bulls---. He's sold us out for Trump hotels in Gaza beach. He's profited off the war machine and oil shorting b-lls--t. My a--h--e's got less money."
